blogs.title: Hawaii’s Long Shadow: The Ninth Circuit Reaffirms Expansive 1182(f) Power in Pacito v. Trump
blogs.description: Explores how the panel leans on Trump v. Hawaii to conclude the President is likely to prevail in suspending refugee entries under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f). Analyzes the court’s refusal to conduct a “searching inquiry” into presidential findings, the breadth of the statute’s text, and what this signals for future challenges to entry restrictions that collide with detailed INA sub-schemes like the Refugee Act.

blogs.title: When “Authorized” Becomes “Required”? Parsing § 1522 and the Refugee Services Mandate
blogs.description: Dissects the panel’s view that 8 U.S.C. § 1522 imposes enforceable duties to provide reception and placement services to refugees already admitted, contrasted with Judge Lee’s dissent that the statute is permissive. Examines textual cues (“shall,” “authorized,” “to the extent of available appropriations”), structural context across subsections (a)–(e), and legislative history to assess whether there is law to apply for APA purposes.

blogs.title: Presidential Orders, Agency Action, and the APA: How Pacito Channels Review Through Implementing Agencies
blogs.description: Analyzes the doctrinal move to avoid direct APA review of the President while policing agency implementation. Evaluates whether terminating cooperative agreements is final agency action, the applicability of Heckler v. Chaney’s discretion bar, and whether § 1522 supplies manageable standards. Discusses the court’s unusual interim remedy—ordering reinstatement of agreements—and how it fits within § 706(1) and 706(2) frameworks.

blogs.title: A Stay With Strings: Tailoring Interim Relief to Preserve Statutory Entitlements
blogs.description: Examines the panel’s use of Nken’s factors to grant a broad stay of the injunctions while carving out a mandatory services obligation for already-admitted refugees. Assesses the institutional and remedial implications of conditioning a stay on reinstating cooperative agreements, and whether this approach could become a model for balancing national security deference with protection of statutory rights during expedited appeals.

blogs.title: The Purse Versus the Pen: Can the Executive Zero Out a Funded Refugee Services Program?
blogs.description: Explores the tension between appropriated funds for refugee assistance and executive attempts to suspend or terminate domestic resettlement services. Considers the “to the extent of available appropriations” clause, the cited appropriations and rescissions, and whether refusal to operate a mandatory program raises Impoundment Control Act concerns. Evaluates how the panel’s order pressures the executive to obligate funds consistent with statutory mandates.

blogs.title: Two Tracks, Two Doctrines: Entry Suspensions vs. Domestic Resettlement Obligations
blogs.description: Highlights the court’s bifurcated approach—deference on entry under § 1182(f) but scrutiny on post-entry services under § 1522. Discusses how immigration-at-the-border doctrines diverge from domestic benefit-delivery rules, and what this means for litigants designing challenges that separate entry restrictions from downstream statutory obligations to persons already in the United States.

blogs.title: Cooperative Agreements as a Litigation Battleground: Grants, Procurement, and Judicial Mandates
blogs.description: Unpacks the legal character of State Department cooperative agreements for reception and placement, distinguishing them from procurement contracts, and considers the court’s authority to require their reinstatement pending appeal. Addresses practical questions about re-competes, continuity of services, and the line between judicial enforcement of statutory duties and micromanagement of program administration.

blogs.title: Harmonizing the Refugee Act with 1182(f): How Much Room Is Left for Congress’s Framework?
blogs.description: Assesses whether a global moratorium on refugee admissions under § 1182(f) can coexist with the Refugee Act’s detailed admissions and consultation scheme. Surveys arguments for reading the statutes in pari materia, the risk of rendering the Refugee Act’s annual ceiling and consultation process an empty formality, and potential limiting principles future courts might deploy to cabin presidential suspension power.

blogs.title: From Travel Bans to Program Halts: The Trajectory of Judicial Review in National Security Immigration
blogs.description: Places Pacito in the broader arc from the 2017 travel ban cases to present. Tracks the consolidation of presidential deference at the border alongside a persistent judicial willingness to enforce statutory constraints on domestic implementation via the APA. Forecasts litigation targets likely to remain viable—service delivery, benefits administration, and grantmaking—even when entry policies receive maximal deference.
